finding: Runner-sync publication can deadlock after a clean build deletes stale release artifacts: the sealed output inventory enumerates existing runner outputs but omits deletion entries, so runner-sync release classifies those deleted publication paths as extra output and returns ATM_RUNNER_PUBLICATION_INVENTORY_INCOMPLETE. The ATM git emergency wrapper also checks task write-ticket scope before honoring hook-bypass approval, so it cannot commit the runner publication surfaces that runner-sync itself requires.
expectedBehavior: Runner-sync inventory should model create, modify, and delete publication operations as first-class sealed members, and the governed emergency path should either consume a runner-sync/steward publication lease or fail with a specific runner-publication-scope error plus a bounded recovery command.
evidenceOrRepro: ATM-GOV-0244 runner-sync receipt .atm/history/evidence/ATM-GOV-0244.runner-sync-receipt.json had 5281 owned-current entries and finalizable lifecycle, but `node atm.mjs broker runner-sync release --task ATM-GOV-0244 --steward-work-id runner-sync-bc38adb2 --receipt-ref .atm/history/evidence/ATM-GOV-0244.runner-sync-receipt.json --json` failed with ATM_RUNNER_PUBLICATION_INVENTORY_INCOMPLETE because five deleted release/atm-root-drop *.d.ts paths were outside the inventory. `node atm.mjs git commit ... --no-verify --emergency-approval lease-6759c3522c74` then failed earlier with ATM_WRITE_TICKET_SCOPE_VIOLATION for runner publication surfaces, requiring a raw path-bounded emergency commit 34f50a551.
followUp: Open a generic runner-sync publication contract card: include deletion entries in runner build inventories, add tests for deleted release artifacts, and provide a governed runner-publication commit/lease path that does not require raw git when the human has approved emergency recovery.
